newsitem.title: UK: Record number of centenarians take to the skies.
newsitem.headline: Record number of centenarians take to the skies.

text.p: Seventy of northern Europe's oldest citizens flew from Antwerp to London on Friday on a promotional trip for the young at heart but 100-plus in age.

Arriving at a London hotel in six coaches and a police escort, the centenarians alighted with slightly confused, almost giddy expressions as a pack of television cameras and microphones engulfed them. A kilt-wearing bagpiper only added to the cacophony.

"It was just wonderful," chirped Caroline Ladd over the noise as she rested in a wheelchair after the hot coach ride from the airport. "I'll be 101 in two weeks," the south Londoner boasted after her companion said that for her 100th birthday Ladd had taken a helicopter ride.
Belgian airline Sabena sponsored the trip to mark Mothers' Day national holiday in Belgium and in the process set a world record for the number of over-100s ever to fly on one aircraft -- 46.
The group, born before the aeroplane itself, was split between three different flights to make room for the two carers that accompanied each centenarian.

The idea for the flight arose after a former Sabena stewardess asked if she could take her mother to London as a 100th birthday present. "We decided to see if there were any more centenarians out there interested in a trip," said Etienne de Nil, Sabena managing director in Britain.
Each flight had a doctor and two nurses on board. To qualify for the free trip, passengers had to have signed letters from their doctors certifying they were fit to fly.

About 30 British centenarians took up the offer and flew to Antwerp on Thursday, joining up with 40 of their fellow century-club members from Belgium, The Netherlands and Germany for Friday's return flight.
The non-Britons were to fly back Friday afternoon after a sightseeing tour of London.

"I've flown many times," said an energetic Ella Scotchmer, who bounded unaided into the hotel, seemingly unfazed by all the attention. "For my next trip I'm going down the Rhine," the 103-year-old Briton added.
Ko Houte Pen from Hoedekenskerke, The Netherlands smiled after his first plane ride in his 100 years and said in Dutch: "It was very good. London looks just like home."
